lines.trans: One of Ms. Cindy's closest friends is about to arrive right here.
My best friend? Who is it—who is this best friend of mine coming here today?
I cannot reveal that to you yet.
Older sister Christine from Pinky4?
Buzzer—wrong! I still cannot tell you.
Wait, surely not CEO Byun?! Is it her? I am calling off this shoot—I cannot work like this!
It is not CEO Byun.
Phew, thank goodness then!
Please name a best friend you usually think of, or a friend you really hope comes today.
Singling out just one person feels awkward—I have so many friends that the others might feel left out.
Honestly, I am dying of curiosity myself.

meanings.note: Used in -(으)ㄴ/는 것 같다 to express 'it seems that...' or 'I think...'.

meanings.en: to be the same, to be like
meanings.note: Compares two things with -와/과 같다.

examples.trans: I think I'm late.
It looks like it's going to rain.

meanings.note: Bound noun often contracted to 거 in everyday speech.

examples.trans: This is my bag.
Because I think I'm late.

meanings.note: Honorific equivalent of 있다; used in 안녕히 계세요 ('goodbye' to someone staying).

examples.trans: Goodbye! (to someone staying)
Is the teacher inside right now?

meanings.en: to be curious; to wonder about
meanings.note: Descriptive adjective in Korean; the thing wondered about takes -이/가.

examples.trans: I'm really curious about the result.
If you have anything you're curious about, please ask.

meanings.note: Colloquial contraction of 그것

examples.trans: Where did you buy that?
That is a really good idea.

meanings.note: Used as polite agreement (그러게요,).

examples.text: 그러게요, 이제 보고 싶은 엄마도 없고 가고 싶은 집도 없고 나 참 많이 변한 것 같아요.
examples.trans: Indeed—now I have no mother I long to see and no home I want to return to; I really have changed a lot.

examples.text: 그러게요. 탁 피디님이 일부러 그러신 건 아닌 거 아는데요, 다리만 좀 멀쩡했어도 상황이 훨씬 나았을 텐데.
examples.trans: Tell me about it. I know Producer Tak did not do it on purpose, yet if only my leg were fine, things would be way better.

meanings.note: Colloquial contraction of 그러면.

examples.trans: Then let's meet tomorrow.
Then we're at the same company!

그렇다.gloss: to be so, to do so

meanings.en: to be like that, to be so
meanings.note: ㅎ-irregular; also used as a pro-verb ('do so / say so')

examples.trans: Is that really so?
Don't keep acting like that.

meanings.note: Emphasizes necessity or strong intention.
Used with holding or closing actions.

examples.trans: Definitely contact me tomorrow.
Please close the door tightly.

meanings.note: Plain first-person singular pronoun used with friends, younger people, or subordinates; contracts to 난 with -는 and becomes 내가 before -가.

examples.trans: I'm going to stay home today.
I'll go first.

meanings.note: Used as noun (나머지).

examples.text: 누구 하나를 꼭 찍기가 좀 그런 게 제가 친구가 많은데 나머지 친구들이 좀 섭섭해할 것 같아서요.
examples.trans: Singling out just one person feels awkward—I have so many friends that the others might feel left out.
This point about the remaining is really important.

meanings.note: interrogative pronoun; becomes 누가 before subject particle -가
indefinite pronoun

examples.trans: Did someone come outside?
Who is that person?
Did you hear about this is fortunate?
I was busy today because of is fortunate.
He is our company's president.
I will speak as the representative.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.text: 1박 팀 아직 도착도 안 했는데 너는 그런 소식을 어디서 그렇게 재빠르게 접했냐?
examples.trans: The 2 Days & 1 Night team has not even arrived back yet—where did you pick up that news so fast?
Here the word for 'even arrival' is key.

meanings.note: Used as game-show interjection (땡,).

examples.trans: Buzzer—wrong! I still cannot tell you.
Buzzer (wrong), it is really nice to see you.

meanings.en: to be many, numerous, or abundant
meanings.note: Used for both countable and uncountable nouns.

examples.trans: Because it's the weekend, there are many people at the department store.

examples.text: 오늘 해야 할 일이 너무 많다.
examples.trans: There is too much work to do today.
I want to humbly tell him right now.
How about trying to humbly tell him together tomorrow?

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (verb).

examples.trans: Yes, ma'am, I am free to talk—please go ahead.
This expression comes from 'please speak'.

맞다.gloss: to be right, to be correct

meanings.note: Used to confirm facts or answers.

meanings.en: to fit, to suit, to match
meanings.note: E.g., 사이즈가 맞다 ('the size fits').

examples.trans: Yes, that's my phone number.
These shoes fit my feet perfectly.

meanings.note: Placed before a verb to express inability or impossibility.

examples.text: 어제는 너무 피곤해서 잠을 못 잤어요.
examples.trans: I was so tired yesterday that I couldn't sleep.
Because it rained, we couldn't go on the picnic.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.text: 네가 회식 가면 본인이 뭐가 되냐고.
examples.trans: She asked what that would make her look like if you showed up at the dinner.
Here the word for 'she herself' is key.

meanings.note: Honorific noun and counter for people, used instead of 사람.

examples.trans: That person over there is our teacher.
How many people are in your party?
Let's I think together today.
I worked hard to I think yesterday too.

examples.text: 선? 검사? 설마 검사가 예쁘기까지 하겠어?
examples.trans: A blind date? A prosecutor? Could a prosecutor really be pretty too?

examples.text: 설마 준비하면 좋은 결과가 있을 거예요.
examples.trans: If we prepare (surely not, could it be), we will get good results.

meanings.note: Used as prospective adnominal (섭섭해할).

examples.text: 누구 하나를 꼭 찍기가 좀 그런 게 제가 친구가 많은데 나머지 친구들이 좀 섭섭해할 것 같아서요.
examples.trans: Singling out just one person feels awkward—I have so many friends that the others might feel left out.
Let us do that (feel hurt) right away.

meanings.note: Bound noun used in -(으)ㄹ 수 있다/없다 ('can / cannot').

examples.trans: I can read Korean.
I cannot go today.
Did you hear about this Ms.?
I was busy today because of Ms..

meanings.note: Expresses sudden realization, surprise, or hesitation.

examples.trans: Ah, yes.
Oh, I see!

meanings.note: Negative copula used with nouns (often with -이/가)

examples.trans: It is not my fault.
Today is not Sunday, it's Monday.

meanings.note: Used in standard farewells 안녕히 계세요 and 안녕히 가세요.

examples.trans: Goodbye! (to someone staying)
Goodbye! (to someone leaving)

meanings.note: Used as humble prospective adnominal (알려드릴).

examples.trans: Buzzer—wrong! I still cannot tell you.
Let us do that (let you know) right away.
Did you hear about this older sister, idol?
I was busy today because of older sister, idol.

없다.gloss: to not exist, to not have

meanings.en: to not exist, to not be present

examples.trans: I don't have time right now.
The tickets are all sold out, so there aren't any.

meanings.note: Often used directly without a locative particle to mean 'here'.

examples.trans: Please sit here.
Here is our office.

meanings.note: The present day; often used adverbially without a particle.

examples.trans: The weather is nice today.
What day of the week is it today?

meanings.en: to come (of a feeling, state, or weather)
meanings.note: Used in expressions like 혼란이 오다 (confusion comes) or 비가 오다 (rain falls)

examples.text: 한국에 온 지 일 년 됐어요.
examples.trans: It's been one year since I came to Korea.
I suddenly started feeling sleepy.

meanings.note: Used as conditional -었으면 (와줬으면).

examples.text: 본인이 평상시에 생각하는 절친이나 오늘 꼭 와줬으면 좋겠다 하는 친구를 말씀해 주세요.
examples.trans: Please name a best friend you usually think of, or a friend you really hope comes today.
Let us do that (wished would come) right away.

meanings.note: Used as pronoun + directional (이곳으로).

examples.text: 이곳으로 신디 씨의 절친 한 분이 도착을 하실 겁니다.
examples.trans: One of Ms. Cindy's closest friends is about to arrive right here.
This point about to this place is really important.

Test2

meanings.note: Humble first-person singular pronoun used in polite speech.

examples.trans: I have an induction ceremony.
Follow me.

meanings.note: Used as slang noun + plural (절친들).

examples.text: 이번에 출연자들 각자 절친들 집에 초대하는 거, 신디 팔로잉을 승찬이 보내볼까?
examples.trans: Still, for the segment where cast members invite best friends home, should we send Seung-chan to follow Cindy?

examples.text: 밖에 1박 팀에서 오늘 절친 특집 관찰 카메라 한다고 찾아왔어.
examples.trans: The 2 Days & 1 Night crew is outside saying they are filming an observation camera for the Best Friends Special today.

접다.gloss: to fold, to wrap up, to shut down

meanings.en: to wrap up, to shut down, to give up (a project or business)
meanings.note: Colloquial/figurative sense.

examples.trans: Fold the paper in half.
Let's just scrap this project.
Please give me some water.
Please wait just a moment.

meanings.note: Contraction of 조금

좋다.gloss: to be good, to be nice

examples.trans: I feel really good today.
It's nice to take a walk in the morning.
Test
Test2

meanings.note: Used colloquially as an adverb meaning 'truly'.
Also used as a noun.

examples.trans: It's seriously cold today.
I thank you sincerely.

meanings.en: to film, to shoot, to take (a photo)
meanings.note: Used for capturing photos or video.
Also means to stamp a seal or dip food into sauce.

examples.trans: Did you happen to film this just now too?
May I take a photo here?
Did you hear about this filming too?
I was busy today because of filming too.

meanings.note: Primary meaning: a friend or peer.

meanings.en: that person / kid (referring to someone younger)
meanings.note: Older speakers often refer to a younger person or celebrity as 그 친구.

examples.trans: I watched a movie with a friend today.
That kid really sings well.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.text: 피곤해 보이는 안색과 눈의 핏줄 상태로 봐선 평상시보다 과음한 게 맞는 것 같고요.
examples.trans: Judging by his exhausted complexion and bloodshot eyes, he definitely drank more heavily than usual.
Here the word for 'than usual' is key.

meanings.note: Native Korean numeral; shortens to 한 before a counter noun (한 개, 한 명).

examples.trans: One coffee, please.
How much is one?

meanings.en: to do, to perform, to hold
meanings.note: Core verb; also combines with nouns to form verbs.

examples.trans: What are you doing right now?
We are holding a meeting today.

meanings.note: Determiner form of 하나, used before a noun counter.

examples.trans: one person
one hour

meanings.note: Softens a question or expresses uncertainty.

examples.trans: Did you happen to film this just now too?
Do you happen to have time?
